abstract: Searches for imaginary quadratic fields with large $\ell$-rank force classes of order $\ell$ through small representations $4m^\ell=y^2+Dz^2$ and pay one class-group computation per candidate. For $\ell=3$, Mestre–Nagao scores of Mordell curves are the classical cheap predictor of extra rank; their extension to $\ell\ge5$ is listed as open by Bagshaw, Jacobson, Rollick and Scheidler. We study what such scores detect, for $\ell=3,5,7,11$. We use 200,000 random fields with $D\in[10^9,10^{10}]$ and a 199,979-field replication. Heuristic class groups serve as ground truth, validated by recomputation (999/999) and exact certification of $r_3\ge2$ for 200 fields. The score of $E_{-16D}:y^2=x^3-16D$ separates $r_3=1$ from $r_3=0$ (Welch $z=15$) and enriches $r_3\ge2$ about 25-fold in its top 0.1%. Quadratic twists of curves with rational $\ell$-torsion are null, including 27a, whose twist $E_{-16D^3}$ shares the class-group part of the Selmer structure. Integral points of $y^2=x^\ell-4^{\ell-1}Dz^2$ with $4\mid x$ correspond to representations $4m^\ell=y^2+Dz^2$. Fields with such a point score 1.2–1.7 SD higher. Imprimitive points without class-group content raise the score equally, and small points carry the mean signal and 64–72% of the top-tail hits. The point frequency, heuristically $D^{1/\ell-1/2}z^{2/\ell-1}$, tracks the decay over cubic twists $z=1,\dots,7$ and the nulls at $z=D,D^2$. Without small points, however, the Mordell score still enriches $r_3\ge2$ 4–13-fold in its tail, and representations with larger $m$ or $z\le13$ do not explain this. For $\ell=5,7$ the point mechanism reappears (+1.3, +0.8 SD), but points are rare (0.27% and 0.06% of fields with $r_\ell=1$) and no residual tail is detected. We do not test filters inside pair-search pipelines and make no claim about target search costs.

change_summary:
Supplement-only fix after desk rejection of XHlTR0edBySyq87k: removed the stray helper build_suppdata.py, which wrote to hard-coded absolute paths and is not part of the workflow. Removed the absolute sys.path entries in gen_fund.py and test_forms.py (now relative to the script directory). The documented workflow (run_all.sh) writes only inside ./work, and tables_rev.py writes only the three subset lists under runs/ relative to the working directory (stated in the README). The manuscript is unchanged from XHlTR0edBySyq87k, whose full change summary relative to 1iHX2ppcjui1hTYL follows.

Revision addressing the review of submission 1iHX2ppcjui1hTYL.
(1) Tails: added Table 2 tail-exceedance columns and a new Section 4.3 / Table 4. As the reviewer found, fields with r3=2 and no z=1 point retain tail enrichment (top 1% x4.3, top 0.1% x12.9 within no-point fields). Representations with larger m (<=1e6) or 2<=z<=13 do NOT explain it (similar base rates). The claims 'no detectable trace' and 'adds essentially no information' are withdrawn. The paper now states that small points carry the mean signal and 64-72% of top-tail hits, and that the Mordell score has a residual tail signal beyond bounded small representations. For l=5,7 no residual tail is detected.
(2) Scope: all search-cost conclusions removed. The abstract and Sections 1, 5 and 6 state explicitly that pipeline-conditioned candidates, cost comparisons, other statistics, larger D and l=13 were not tested, and make no claim about target search costs. Added discussion of [19] (Bujanovic-Kazalicki-Novak) and [20] (Bujanovic-Kazalicki-Vlah).
(3) Statistics: all z-scores recomputed as Welch statistics (headline 20.3 -> 15.4, 17.7 -> 13.6). Effect sizes are Glass's delta with Welch SE. Stratified effects use sample-size weights and equal the raw effects (0.0736/0.0737; 0.312/0.311), and the incorrect 'quarter of the signal is 3-adic' claim is removed. Replication z-scores recomputed (14.4/12.4).
(4) Implementation: bad primes now excluded for all fixed curves (conductor primes removed from trace tables); Table 1 regenerated, and the quadratic-twist families remain null. A new counter (smallpts2.c) classifies EVERY representation as primitive or imprimitive, including the even-D case (4|D, 4|y), which the old check missed. Fields with both kinds (92) are handled explicitly.
(5) Validation: recomputation of h and ranks with Pmax=1e6 for 999 sampled-range fields, including all 94 high-score tail fields and non-cyclic 3-Sylow cases: 999/999 agree. Exact certification of r3>=2 by form arithmetic for 200 fields, including all 94 tail fields: 200/200. No r3=0 field has a primitive z in {1,2} representation. The claim that heuristic errors 'would only blur signals' is removed.
(1b) Replication of the residual tail (as requested): within 195,640 replication fields without a z=1 point the score enriches r3>=2 x4.4 (top 1%) and x10.9 (top 0.1%), p<1e-15.
(6) Reproducibility: full driver run_all.sh (seeds, sharding, overlap removal, probe and tail subsets, validation, analysis), plus larger data files (all r3>=2 fields, 5,000 main and 2,000 replication random fields, subset lists).
title: What Mestre–Nagao scores detect about ℓ-ranks of imaginary quadratic fields: small representations and a residual tail (ℓ = 3, 5, 7, 11)
